procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit from her office over lunch, rescheduled from the missed December appt. 23 wks. OB seeing her every 2-3 wks given last pregnancy; she says all checks have been normal and the baby is growing fine.

Anxiety: more on her mind this time - keeps thinking about last May, worries every time she feels any wetness. Sleeping ok most nights. Working full time. No panic attacks. Not depressed. GAD-7 8, PHQ-9 4. Taking sertraline 50 daily, levothyroxine 88, prenatal.

Obs: well appearing on video, speaking easily, appropriate affect, a bit anxious when talking about the last delivery.

A/P
1. GAD with pregnancy-related worry - talked through what she can watch for and when to call L&D, which seemed to help. Offered to increase sertraline to 75 or a therapy referral; she wants to hold for now and will message if it gets worse. Continue 50.
2. Hypothyroidism - OB has been checking TSH; asked her to have them send results. Continue 88.
3. IDA - on prenatal with iron.
Follow up after delivery.

documents.title: Obstetrics Visit Note
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Prenatal visit 02/17/2026 at 28w2d. G2P0101. Hx PPROM at 35 wks with intra-amniotic infection.
No leakage of fluid, bleeding or contractions. Good fetal movement.
Fundal height appropriate for dates, fetal heart tones normal. Anatomy survey at 20 wks normal; growth scan this month normal, fluid normal.
Tdap 0.5 mL IM L deltoid today.
TSH from last month in range, copy to PCP.
Meds: levothyroxine 88 mcg, sertraline 50 mg, PNV with iron, docusate prn. Allergies: penicillin (anaphylaxis), latex.
Plan: continue close follow-up; reviewed signs of rupture of membranes and preterm labor.

documents.title: Refills
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, can I get my levothyroxine and sertraline refilled for 3 months? I want to have plenty on hand before the baby comes. Same pharmacy. Thanks!

documents.title: RE: Refills
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Both sent to your pharmacy, 90 days with a refill. Good luck these last weeks!

documents.title: Delivery Note
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Date of service: 05/03/2026

29 y/o G2P0101 at 39w0d (EDD 05/10/2026) admitted in spontaneous labor at 02:40. Prenatal care began early and this pregnancy has been uncomplicated. History of PPROM with intra-amniotic infection at 35 weeks in 2025. Allergies: penicillin (anaphylaxis), latex - latex-free room.

Spontaneous vaginal delivery at 08:12 of a full-term male infant. Amniotic fluid clear.

Newborn: good tone and a strong cry at birth. Cord clamped and cut; infant placed on mother's abdomen. Pink initially, then mild central cyanosis by the end of the first minute. HR 140, RR 50 with good respiratory effort, active muscle tone, crying vigorously. Warm room; infant dried and stimulated with back rubbing. Cyanosis resolved with routine care by 5 minutes. Term infant to routine newborn care with the pediatric team.

Placenta delivered spontaneously, intact. EBL within normal limits. Mother stable.

documents.title: Obstetric Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Admission: 05/03/2026   Discharge: 05/05/2026

Diagnosis: term pregnancy at 39 weeks 0 days, delivered by spontaneous vaginal delivery. Obstetric history now G2P1102.

Course: admitted in spontaneous labor, uncomplicated labor and delivery on 05/03/2026 of a term male infant (see delivery note). Postpartum course routine: afebrile, fundus firm, lochia appropriate, ambulating and voiding, pain controlled.

PMH: generalized anxiety disorder, hypothyroidism, iron deficiency anemia.
Discharge medications (unchanged from home): levothyroxine 88 mcg daily; sertraline 50 mg daily; prenatal vitamin with iron daily; docusate 100 mg as needed.
Allergies: penicillin (anaphylaxis); latex (contact dermatitis).

Follow-up: obstetrics postpartum visit in 6 weeks. Primary care within 1-2 weeks for thyroid, mood and anemia follow-up.

documents.title: Post-Discharge Phone Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Spoke with pt, day 3 after term SVD 5/3, home 5/5. Feels "a lot better than last time." No fever. Bleeding moderate and decreasing. No headache, vision changes, chest pain or leg swelling. Taking her usual meds, no new ones. Mood good, tired. Reviewed when to call. PCP visit booked 5/12.

orders.reason: Iron deficiency anemia, recheck in 3 months

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
9 days after term SVD (5/3, 39 wks, boy). Uncomplicated labor and delivery, home 5/5. Delivery note and discharge summary reviewed. Med rec - same four meds, nothing new.

Doing well. Bleeding light. Sore but improving. No fever, no urinary symptoms. Sleep is in pieces. Mood "honestly better than last year" - some worry, no low mood, no thoughts of self-harm. GAD-7 7, PHQ-9 5.

Exam: vitals as charted. Tired but well appearing. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, uterus not palpable above the symphysis. Calves non-tender. Affect bright.

A/P
1. Postpartum, term SVD - routine recovery. OB postpartum visit mid-June.
2. GAD - stable on sertraline 50, continue. She knows to reach out if mood changes in the coming weeks.
3. Hypothyroidism - TSH today, continue 88.
4. IDA - CBC/ferritin today. Continue prenatal with iron.
Physical due this fall; Pap due this year.

documents.title: Obstetrics Postpartum Visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Postpartum visit 06/16/2026, 6 weeks after term spontaneous vaginal delivery.

No complaints. Bleeding has stopped. No pelvic pain, urinary or bowel problems. Mood stable on sertraline.
Exam: BP normal. Abdomen soft. Perineum healed. Uterus involuted, non-tender.

Assessment: normal postpartum recovery. G2P1102.
Medications: levothyroxine 88 mcg, sertraline 50 mg, prenatal vitamin with iron, docusate PRN. Allergies: penicillin (anaphylaxis), latex.
Cervical screening due this year - deferred to primary care per patient preference.
Return to primary care for ongoing care.
